messages:
morgan: ran nsys+perfetto on the kv-cache hot path on dedicated-2; kernel timelines look sane but most C++ frames show no file/line — everything collapses to <unknown> or address-only. attached qdrep at /tmp/kvtrace.qdrep, any ideas?

samir: quick check — were the binaries in the container stripped? a lot of our release images run a chroot/pack step that drops /usr/lib/debug.

morgan: build job includes -g, but final image does a multistage copy and we do a strip in the final stage. i pulled the binary out and `readelf --notes` shows a build-id, but the container filesystem has no /usr/lib/debug/.build-id tree. maybe nsys/perfetto can't find the separate debug info.

jess: also watch CUPTI version mismatch. nsight/nsys rely on CUPTI to resolve kernel names and sometimes user frames if the lib paths don't match. if the container has a different libcupti.so than the host driver expects, mappings get weird.

oliver: can you paste the exact nsys command you used? and does nvprof show the same?
morgan: i ran:```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx -o /tmp/kvtrace ./redwood-runtime --run-profile
# then convert to qdrep/perfetto and open in Nsight
```nvprof shows similar: a bunch of kernel blocks with no symbolic info for our runtime frames.

samir: quick repro steps that helped me previously:
1) run the same binary on host (not in container) with the host's /usr/lib/debug mounted, see if symbols appear.
2) if yes, it's a build-id / debug-info lookup issue. `eu-readelf --debug-dump=info your_binary` to check debug sections.
3) try mounting host's /usr/lib/debug into the container: `-v /usr/lib/debug:/usr/lib/debug:ro` then re-run nsys.

(works as a temporary diagnostic)

jess: another gotcha — some of our Dockerfiles install libcupti from the CUDA toolkit inside the image, but the kernel driver on the node expects a different CUPTI ABI. For full stack mapping nsight needs the matching CUPTI and sometimes access to /proc/driver/nvidia. Mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so from the host into container helped me once.

morgan: mounted /usr/lib/debug and swapped libcupti (bind mount host libcupti.so into /usr/local/cuda/lib64) — trace then showed file/line for a subset of frames. progress. still missing a few inlined or optimized frames.

oliver: optimization/inlining will make some line info disappear unless you keep full debug info and avoid -fomit-frame-pointer etc. for profiling builds we usually: `-g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer` then produce a separate debug package (strip binary but keep debug in .debug files and populate /usr/lib/debug/.build-id).

morgan: thanks. two action items: 1) update the Docker build to produce and persist a debug-info package and avoid blind stripping in the final image; 2) ensure CI profiling images bind host CUPTI or use driver-matching CUPTI packages. i'll open a PR for the Dockerfile changes and a short runbook for debugging traces.

buildbot: created issue #1243: "chrooted images: missing build-id debug info -> nsys/perfetto unresolved frames" (assigned morgan).

samir: if you need a quick command to locate build id mapping: `objdump --private-headers your_binary | grep 'Build ID'` and `find /usr/lib/debug/.build-id -type f | sed -n '1,10p'` to confirm presence.

morgan: i'll try to reproduce end-to-end on a fresh node and then post before/after qdreps. thanks all :thumbsup:
